resources.string: Screenly reads permitted on-screen labels, control states, app identity, and positions to help you navigate other applications. This access can reveal sensitive content. Extraction stays on your device, but debug builds may print sanitized metadata to Logcat. Screenly does not upload the extracted data or automatically tap controls.
I understand and agree to Screenly accessing permitted on-screen UI information.
Access enabled. Ready to inspect Android Settings.
In Accessibility Settings, open Downloaded apps or Installed services, select Screenly, and turn on Use Screenly. Return here to check the status.

Test: Open Android Settings, tap the Screenly bubble, then Explain. In a debug build, review extracted nodes, labels, IDs, clickable states, and bounds. Tap a row to expand its metadata. Use Refresh screen after navigating. Guide Me still supports manual highlighting.

Screen observations are transient, with sanitized labels in debug Logcat. Password and sensitive subtrees are skipped, and editable values are omitted. No network permission or automatic taps. Disable access at any time in Android Accessibility Settings; you can also withdraw in-app consent here.

Inspects accessible interface elements in other apps and displays a floating assistant for manual highlighting. Debug observations appear in Logcat. Password and sensitive nodes are skipped, and editable values are omitted. No screen contents are saved or sent over the network; Screenly does not tap for you.
Screenly assistant. Tap to open actions; drag to move.
On-device AI chat is not available in this prototype yet. Use Guide Me to manually select and highlight controls.
AI screen explanations are not implemented yet. Guide Me can highlight a selected control without tapping it for you.
No enabled clickable elements are available on this screen. Close the picker and navigate to another screen.
The screen changed. Open the picker again to select a current element.
Visible items on your current screen
What would you like to do?
Screenly checks your current screen and suggests one step at a time.
What Screenly can access and how it handles data
Captures happen only when requested. There is no continuous screen recording.
Screen images are released from memory after each request and are not saved or uploaded. Chat text is stored only in memory until cleared or the service stops.
Vision model not connected. Accessibility-based assistance works offline. The text-only model is on a separate development branch.
Accessibility service enabled. Screenshot access requires the accessibility capture capability to be approved.
No screenshots stored. Pending capture cancelled.
Hiding Screenly and capturing the current view...
The current app screen is unavailable.
Screen captured locally and discarded. Only accessibility labels were interpreted; no vision model is connected.
Capture failed or this screen is protected. No screenshot was analyzed.
Screenshot permission unavailable. Check Screenly in Accessibility Settings.
